records.mutation: replace passive no-case-split warning with explicit merged-reading move plus contradiction-loop tripwire
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored 0 (train 0.000) and 5 of 8 hit the 16384-token cap with nothing committed. Every rollout that reasoned visibly did the one thing the incumbent warned against in the abstract: it pinned the reveal to sum, then to product, derived a contradiction in both branches (one rollout wrote "impossible" 70 times), and then thrashed or guessed. The edit turns that passive warning into an executable merged-candidate-list move and adds a concrete tripwire (repeated "impossible" means the knowledge model is wrong), while leaving the proven announcement-filtering and commit-and-stop clauses intact.

records.mutation: widen trigger from phrasing-based to structural; drop unused Apollonius label
records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts scored 8/8 with every sample terminating normally (finish_reason stop, 3.8k-6.9k of 16384 tokens), so train accuracy has no headroom and any risk to the proven body is pure downside. Keyword scans show the students reliably execute the take-moduli first move, the k^n=|c| check, complete-the-square, and the original-equation verification, but only one of eight ever used the 'Apollonius' label, making it dead weight. I therefore made one generality edit - replacing the phrasing-dependent trigger 'For all roots lie on one circle problems' with the structural condition 'an equation equates two n-th powers of linear expressions in z' so the hint fires on locus/center/radius variants that never use the word circle - and paid for it by deleting the unused label, leaving the hint slightly shorter than the incumbent (195 vs 198 tokens).

records.mutation: cut unused proof/minimization clauses, add explicit no-rewrite termination rule
records.subagent_summary: All 8 rollouts ran 15k-16.4k tokens and 6 of 8 truncated at the 16384 cap; both successes stopped early, so the binding constraint is budget, not geometry. Failures share two visible patterns: they never attempt the 'show the far edges are too distant' proof or the 'minimize over the symmetry-reduced range' step the incumbent asks for, and instead loop on qualitative prose arguments about which placement minimizes overlap, then burn the remaining budget re-deriving and typesetting a long formatted write-up after already having a number. So I deleted those two never-followed clauses and spent the tokens on a ban on prose minimality arguments plus an explicit stop-after-one-number rule; net length is slightly shorter than the incumbent.

records.mutation: swap unused differencing warning for the n-vs-n+1 root-cap trap plus a no-downgrade rule
records.subagent_summary: Fresh 8 rollouts gave train 4/8 with zero truncations (all finish_reason stop, 8.4k-11.1k tokens), so the failures are a single reusable counting error, not budget. Every rollout adopted the affine-target/root-bound frame, but two failures set the per-polynomial cap to degree+1 by invoking 'n+1 points determine a degree-n polynomial', one picked an unjustified smaller cap, and one derived the correct cap then downgraded its count at the last step; no rollout ever attempted the finite-differencing dead end my incumbent warned against. I therefore deleted that dead clause and spent the identical token count (161, same as incumbent) on the explicit n-vs-n+1 cap trap and a no-downgrade commit rule, changing nothing else.

records.mutation: make the contradiction-recovery step executable via a numeric check at a given point
records.subagent_summary: 6/8 rollouts scored 1; the only two failures both hit the 16384-token cap with nothing stated, and both looped for the same reason: after inverting one ratio while rewriting the log expression they reached a contradiction (or a negative discriminant), then re-derived the whole setup repeatedly instead of localizing the flip. The incumbent's 'recheck only that conversion line' was too vague to act on, so this edit replaces it with a concrete diagnostic (evaluate the curve numerically at a supplied point and repair only the line that fails) while leaving every other proven clause intact and keeping length essentially flat.

records.mutation: replace unused state-graph clause with the k-intakes-to-depth conversion rule
records.subagent_summary: All 8 rollouts scored 0 with finish_reason stop and no truncation, so budget is not the issue; failures were conceptual. No rollout ever built the 'small state graph' the incumbent asked for, so that clause was dead weight and I deleted it. Six of eight failures came from the same two steps: mistranslating 'bottom of the shed' into a timing claim (some said last delivered, one concluded the target item could never move at all) and then falling back on a uniform-order symmetry claim to produce a bare 1/n, so I spent the freed tokens on an explicit rule converting depth into the number of intake moves preceding the first delivery, and kept the proven anti-symmetry and commit-and-stop wording unchanged.

records.mutation: correct the weights-vs-polynomial-coefficients misreading and ban the two observed derailments
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored 0 and 7 of 8 hit the token cap with nothing committed; every one of them reinterpreted the unknowns as coefficients of a single polynomial in x, then burned the budget expanding elementary-symmetric coefficients, chasing harmonic sums, or hand-checking tiny analogues. The edit keeps the proven functional framing and closing commit rule but adds one clause naming that misreading and replaces the unused 'do not invert/re-index' ban with the two derailments actually observed.

records.mutation: delete unused layout clause; generalize houses to identical units and name gcd
records.subagent_summary: All 8 rollouts were correct and terminated cleanly, so train accuracy cannot rise and the only lever is transfer. Every rollout used the divide-every-stage-total clause and computed a gcd explicitly, but none ever used the equal-street layout clause (they mentioned it and then discarded it), so that clause is dead weight; one rollout burned nearly 7k tokens re-litigating the interpretation before committing. I therefore deleted the unused layout clause, replaced the problem-specific nouns (houses, construction costs) with the general identical-units / cost-components framing, named gcd since the student derives it anyway, and added a short commit-and-stop, keeping the hint no longer than the incumbent.

records.mutation: rename affine shift to a fresh letter; require top-down coefficient matching instead of single-point substitution; drop unused q=p+const branch warning
records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts scored 5/8: the three failures were one truncation (a detour into rational substitution and a huge quadratic, never terminating) and two that reused the same letter for the affine shift and for the polynomial's quadratic coefficient, then substituted a single numeric point instead of matching coefficients, producing wrong coefficients from an underdetermined system. The edit renames the shift constant, makes 'match the top couple of coefficients' concretely top-down with the leading coefficient first, and explicitly bans the single-point shortcut; the branch-warning clause no rollout ever used was deleted to keep length below the incumbent.

records.mutation: replace costly full-list re-verification clause with a single-label index map plus a two-size budget cap
records.subagent_summary: All 8 rollouts scored 0 this round; 7 of 8 terminated with finish_reason=length at the 16384-token cap having committed nothing, and the one that stopped guessed an off-by-one exponent after abandoning its trace. Failures were dominated by repeatedly rewriting full letter lists for n=2 and n=3, then declaring the work 'too complex' and restarting, so I deleted the incumbent's expensive per-stage bookkeeping/redo clause (which visibly fed that loop) and replaced it with an operational cheaper representation: compose the n stages into one index map for a single label and iterate only that map, capped at two sizes. The proven first move, overlap trap, trust-the-trace rule, and commit-and-stop rule are kept, and the hint is shorter than the incumbent (181 vs 190 tokens).
